items.title: Ray Bauduc Interview, 1984-06-27
items.q: I don't know, Harry Shields or Larry Shields or, or, or Branny. There was, you know, they were supposed to be the jazz clowns

ctx.x: Well, I mean, he, he, he would be able to tell you more about it, see. Or, Bill Eastwood. Yeah, I knew him too. Because they, they lived over there in Al Jays, you know, I mean, uh, Eastwood and, and they played, uh, with, uh, well, he played at the halfway house when I was there, see. But, uh, but Emmett, uh, they went on, uh, on a tour. He, I don't, uh, Johnny Frisco drummed up, let's see if I can remember this guy. Johnny Frisco was on drums, Santo, Emmett Hardy, and, uh, I don't know, Harry Shields or Larry…

items.title: Ray Bauduc Interview, 1984-06-26
items.q: That kind of chorus that Larry Shields played.

ctx.x: They were good numbers. They were fine years.

They were good numbers, just like when a guy wants a kid around and play slapsticky. And we played the St. Louis Blues, and they played... That kind of chorus that Larry Shields played. It was a corny figure, you know what I mean? Yeah. I always put that in. But the band that I think that your company there will achieve, the business, Tulane, and this place that's out on the end of Espinade, what is that? The Old Mint.
